Normally the Viewer only attempts to run its own effects (like gain, gamma, and viewer process node) on the GPU. Activate this to also compute nodes connected to the Viewer input on the GPU when possible (not all nodes have a GPU implementation).
If nodes are computed on the GPU, the color values displayed in the Viewer will be inaccurate since they show the color from the last node computed in the CPU prior to transferring the image into the graphics card.

useGPUForInputs.label: use GPU for inputs when possible
useGPUForInputs.name: useGPUForInputs

description.text:
Enable to allow the Viewer to apply its effects (like gain, gamma, and viewer process node) in the GPU when possible.
The 'when possible' exception is due to the fact that in some cases, like when broadcast monitor output is enabled or the GL buffer depth is 8 bit, effects must be computed in the CPU.

The Viewer Process operation is applied to the viewed image before it is displayed on the screen. It is typically used to convert from linear to your monitor's colorspace.

You can use the Python command nuke.ViewerProcess.register() to add more options to this list. See the User Guide for details and find examples in the init.py file in your Nuke installation.
